title: GM-level calculation: quiet and defensive resources
summary: Positions where the solution includes quiet moves for both sides, defensive only-moves and a precise final evaluation.

steps.md:
## What GMs calculate differently

- They find **quiet moves in the middle of forcing lines** (for both sides).
- They see the **defender's only-moves** and calculate them as carefully as their own.
- They **evaluate the end position correctly**: an extra pawn in a drawn ending is a draw; a queen versus rook and two passed pawns is a matter of counting.
- They manage the tree: candidates first, branches once, quiet endpoints.

steps.prompt: Black to move (Larsen-Spassky, Belgrade 1970). A pawn capture that opens everything (Larsen-Spassky, Belgrade URS-World 1970)
steps.explain: **13...hxg3!** — Black opens the h-file; the rook on h8 joins the attack with tempo. Engine main line: 13...hxg3 14.Rg1 Qh4 15.Rg2 Bxg4 16.Qxe4 Qh1+ 17.Bf1 Rhe8 18.Be5. (Larsen-Spassky, Belgrade URS-World 1970; checked with Stockfish 19.)

steps.prompt: Black to move (two moves later, after the famous 14...Rh1!! 15.Rxh1). Finish the attack (Larsen-Spassky, Belgrade URS-World 1970)
steps.explain: **15...g2!** — the pawn attacks the h1-rook and threatens to promote; after 16.Rf1 Qh4+ 17.Kd1 gxf1=Q+ Black wins decisively. Engine main line: 15...g2 16.Rf1 Qh4+ 17.Kd1 gxf1=Q+ 18.Bxf1. (Larsen-Spassky, Belgrade URS-World 1970; checked with Stockfish 19.)

steps.prompt: White to move (Kasparov-Topalov 1999, move 34). The king hunt is almost over. Find the only move (Kasparov-Topalov, Hoogovens 1999)
steps.explain: **34.Qa1+!** — the queen returns with check; only this keeps White winning chances. Engine main line: 34.Qa1+ Kd2 35.Qb2+ Kd1 36.Bf1 Rd2 37.Bxc4 Rxb2+ 38.Kxb2 bxc4. (Kasparov-Topalov, Hoogovens 1999; checked with Stockfish 19.)

steps.prompt: White to move (move 36). A quiet bishop move in the middle of the hunt (Kasparov-Topalov, Hoogovens 1999)
steps.explain: **36.Bf1!!** — the bishop attacks the queen on c4 and deflects it; the black king on d1 is in a net. Engine main line: 36.Bf1 Rd2 37.Rd7 Rxd7 38.Bxc4 bxc4 39.Qxh8 Rd3. (Kasparov-Topalov, Hoogovens 1999; checked with Stockfish 19.)

steps.prompt: White to move (Ding-Nepomniachtchi, World Championship 2023). Break through (Ding Liren-Nepomniachtchi, WCh 2023 2023)
steps.explain: **35.Rxe6!** — the rook takes the e6-pawn, opening the long diagonal and the path of the d-pawn; the engine line shows a decisive attack. Engine main line: 35.Rxe6 f3 36.d5+ Ne5 37.Rxe5 fxg2+ 38.Rxg2 Bxe5 39.Qxe5+ Rhf6. (Ding Liren-Nepomniachtchi, WCh 2023 2023; checked with Stockfish 19.)

steps.question: At the end of a 10-ply line you reach queen and pawn against queen with your king exposed to checks. How do you evaluate it?
choices: Winning: you have an extra pawn
Calculate whether the opponent has perpetual check; with an exposed king, Q+P v Q is often a draw — the evaluation depends on shelter from checks
steps.explain: Final-position evaluation is where many 2400 players go wrong. Know the endgame and count the checks.

steps.md:
## Assignment

- **Calculation drill**: 3 GM Preparation-level positions per week, 30 minutes each, written solution with sidelines; score main line and defences separately.
- **Puzzles**: 15 *superGM* + *defensiveMove* puzzles.
- Re-solve the positions you failed after two weeks.

sources: Larsen-Spassky, USSR v Rest of the World, Belgrade 1970
